threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think ‘south of the river’ means an exciting day trip, not an unspoken rule about loyalty.
Last week on the 59, a guy serenaded the whole bus with Whitney Houston. No one clapped, but everyone smiled. That's Brixton for you.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The sound of a random 'Schwarze Katze' party on the rooftop beside mine—kicking off on a Tuesday night, complete with karaoke. That's when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a kebab shop serving late-night vegan options alongside Turkish tea. That late-night chatter is a true Berlin vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone's a local when they know how to dodge the BART delays and still make it to Dolores Park for sunset.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 21 bus today, driver stopped to let a pigeon cross. Everyone just smiled. Only in SF do we pause for birds.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is just about the Gaudí buildings, but it's the local cafes and daily chat with the baker that define us.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by how they still pause to take photos of every street art piece, while the rest of us just walk by.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'cabbie' instead of a 'taxi'. The locals can spot a newbie just by that slip.
Last night on the 196, a guy was passionately debating whether foggy weather makes you more philosophical. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a flock of starlings perform their nightly dance above Sonnenallee, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin will you find clubs that are open for breakfast. Nothing says night out like a sunrise rave at Sisyphos with a currywurst in hand.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only locals know to steer clear of the taquerias at 5 PM when the line snakes down the block; tourists are all too eager to wait.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a guy serenade the bus stop with an accordion, only to have a pigeon join in, bobbing its head like it understood the beat. Classic San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists flock to Parc Güell, but they miss the little playground tucked behind it where local kids play—much more authentic.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by how they struggle with the metro map—like it’s written in hieroglyphics instead of just Spanish and Catalan.
